To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We targeted oral bioactivity and efficacy against multidrugs resistant tumors in vivo for eribulin analogs.

the design, synthesis and in vitro/in vivo evaluation of novel amide- and urea-containing analogs of the microtubule-targeting agent, eribulin, led to the identification of compounds with improved oral bioavailability, reduced PgP-mediated drug transport, and efficacy against MDR tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of orally bioavailable and active analogs of eriburin mesylate.
the design of novel analogs of eriublin mesylate, which are orally active and active against resistant tumor cells.
the development of orally available and active analogs of erubilin mesylate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amine-containing analogues of eribulin are promising candidates for the treatment of MDR tumors and for oral administration.
the amine-containing analog 2a was the best compound of this series, with the most favorable profile of all the compounds tested.
these compounds are promising candidates for further investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a novel series of eribulin analogs has been designed, synthesized and evaluated.
the amine-containing analogues of eribulin were found to be potent in vitro, orally bioavailable, and active against resistant tumor models in vivo.
the amine-containing eribulin analogs are orally available and active against MDR tumors in vivo, which may be useful for future development of orally available eribulin analog.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the basicity of amino group(s) at C32 of the side-chain region of eribulin can be attenuated without loss of antitumor activity, and this can be used as a tool for the development of orally bioavailable analogs of eriburin.

the basicity of the amine group in the C32 region of eribulin is a critical determinant of the drug’s activity and that the C32 amine group can be modified in order to improve the drug’s oral bioavailability and activity against MDR tumors.
the C32 side chain region of eribulin is a viable site for modification, and that the basicity of the C32 amine group is a major contributor to PgP-mediated efflux.
